## Draft — display only (not executed here)
RevBayes uses the **Rev** language, which does **not** run as a Quarto cell — the code
below is for reading and for pasting into RevBayes. **This practical has not been executed
in this repo.** The authoritative, maintained version (with data files) is the RevBayes
tutorial **[Time-calibrated phylogenetics / `timefig_dating`, Part 1](https://revbayes.github.io/tutorials/timefig_dating/#molecular-phylogenetics)**.
See [`SETUP.md`](SETUP.md) for installing RevBayes + RevGadgets and getting the data.
:::

## Goal

Estimate a **time-calibrated phylogeny** for Hawaiian *Kadua* (Rubiaceae) from molecular
data, and see first-hand why **molecular data alone cannot date a tree** (the rate–time
non-identifiability from the [dating lecture](../02-molecular-dating.qmd)).

**Model pieces** (each a swappable node in the RevBayes graphical model):

- substitution model: **HKY85 + Γ** (per locus),
- **lognormal relaxed clock** (branch-specific rates),
- **constant-rate birth–death** tree prior with a uniform root-age prior,
- **no calibration** (the point: watch the node ages blow up).

## 1. Setup and data

```{.rev}
# --- housekeeping ---
seed(1)
loci    = ["ITS", "ETS"]          # the tutorial ships 10 Angiosperms353 loci; 2 for speed
n_loci  = loci.size()
root_max = 34.0                   # Ma; max age of the Hawaiian high islands + slack

# --- read the alignments ---
for (i in 1:n_loci) {
    data[i] = readDiscreteCharacterData("data/kadua_" + loci[i] + ".nex")
}
taxa    = data[1].taxa()
n_taxa  = taxa.size()

# move/monitor containers
moves    = VectorMoves()
monitors = VectorMonitors()
```

## 2. Tree prior — constant-rate birth–death

```{.rev}
# diversification and turnover -> birth (lambda) and death (mu) rates
diversification ~ dnExponential(10.0)
turnover        ~ dnExponential(10.0)
moves.append( mvScale(diversification, weight=2) )
moves.append( mvScale(turnover,        weight=2) )

speciation := diversification + turnover      # lambda
extinction := turnover                         # mu

# uniform prior on the root age (no calibration -> wide)
root_age ~ dnUniform(0.0, root_max)
moves.append( mvSlide(root_age, weight=2) )

rho = 27.0 / 32.0                              # ~27 of 32 species sampled

timetree ~ dnBDP(lambda=speciation, mu=extinction, rootAge=root_age,
                 rho=rho, taxa=taxa)

# topology moves (comment out & clamp a fixed topology to date only)
moves.append( mvNNI(timetree, weight=n_taxa) )
moves.append( mvFNPR(timetree, weight=n_taxa/4) )
moves.append( mvNodeTimeSlideUniform(timetree, weight=n_taxa) )
```

## 3. Relaxed clock

```{.rev}
# lognormal uncorrelated relaxed clock: one rate per branch
n_branches = 2 * n_taxa - 2
clock_mean ~ dnExponential(10.0)
clock_sd   ~ dnExponential(3.0)
moves.append( mvScale(clock_mean, weight=2) )
moves.append( mvScale(clock_sd,   weight=2) )

for (i in 1:n_branches) {
    branch_rates[i] ~ dnLognormal( ln(clock_mean) - 0.5*clock_sd^2, clock_sd )
    moves.append( mvScale(branch_rates[i], weight=1) )
}
```

## 4. Substitution model (HKY + Γ, per locus)

```{.rev}
for (i in 1:n_loci) {
    # base frequencies and kappa
    pi[i]    ~ dnDirichlet( v(1,1,1,1) )
    kappa[i] ~ dnLognormal(0.0, 1.0)
    moves.append( mvSimplexElementScale(pi[i], weight=2) )
    moves.append( mvScale(kappa[i], weight=2) )
    Q[i] := fnHKY(kappa[i], pi[i])

    # +Gamma4 among-site rate variation
    alpha[i] ~ dnExponential(1.0)
    moves.append( mvScale(alpha[i], weight=2) )
    site_rates[i] := fnDiscretizeGamma(alpha[i], alpha[i], 4)

    # per-locus relative rate multiplier
    mu_locus[i] ~ dnExponential(1.0)
    moves.append( mvScale(mu_locus[i], weight=2) )

    # the phylogenetic CTMC, clamped to the data
    seq[i] ~ dnPhyloCTMC(tree=timetree, Q=Q[i],
                         branchRates=branch_rates * mu_locus[i],
                         siteRates=site_rates[i], type="DNA")
    seq[i].clamp( data[i] )
}
```

## 5. MCMC

```{.rev}
mymodel = model(timetree)

monitors.append( mnModel(filename="output/kadua_divtime.log", printgen=10) )
monitors.append( mnFile(timetree, filename="output/kadua_divtime.trees", printgen=10) )
monitors.append( mnScreen(root_age, diversification, printgen=100) )

mymcmc = mcmc(mymodel, moves, monitors)
mymcmc.run(generations=20000)     # a real run needs far more; check ESS in Tracer

# summarize to a maximum-clade-credibility tree
trace = readTreeTrace("output/kadua_divtime.trees", treetype="clock")
mccTree(trace, file="output/kadua_divtime.mcc.tre")
```

## 6. Visualize (R + RevGadgets)

```{.r}
library(RevGadgets)
tree <- readTrees("output/kadua_divtime.mcc.tre")
plotFBDTree(tree, timeline = TRUE, node_age_bars = TRUE,
            age_bars_colored_by = "posterior") +
  ggplot2::ggtitle("Kadua — uncalibrated divergence times")
```

::: {.figure-prompt}
**FIGURE (student output)** — the MCC chronogram with **node-age bars (95% HPD)** on a time
axis. Expect **very wide** bars: with no calibration the ages are barely constrained.
:::

## The lesson

- The topology and *relative* branch lengths are well estimated, but **absolute node ages
  are not** — the 95% HPD intervals span most of the allowed root range.
- This is **rate–time non-identifiability** in action. Fixing it requires **calibrations**
  (fossils, secondary ages, or **island ages** — the natural move for a Hawaiian radiation).

> **Try it:** add a calibration by replacing the uniform `root_age` with an informative
> prior (e.g. `dnNormal` around an island-age estimate) and re-run. How much do the HPD
> intervals shrink?
